title: Sherpa-UI pattern
description: One UI pattern: for this need, this layout and these components. An agent picks one by its `when`, run over the need, and never invents a layout. Sherpa's patterns and an app's own are each one of these. docs/history/plan-700-agents.md §3

id.description: Its id: an app's pattern of the same id replaces Sherpa's.

use.description: What it is for, in a sentence or two.

when.description: When it fits: conditions on the need, all of which hold.

rank.description: Its place among the patterns that fit: the highest first.

page.description: What it adds to the page definition (page.v1.json): its scopes, and its components' configuration.

states.description: The states of its data it draws: loading; empty, no-matches and error, a container's data-state; unreached and down, its source's reach.

agent.description: What an agent may change, and the roles it keeps.

may.description: A role of its layout, or a part of its page: columns, presets.

keeps.description: Roles of its layout an agent never takes away.

node.description: One element of its layout: a component spec's anatomy node, as a page writes it. A child placed in a slot says so in attrs.slot; a page has no <slot> and no template, so no slot or showWhen.

role.description: What it does in the pattern: what `agent` names.

each.description: One of it for each of the need's fields of this kind.

max.description: At most this many of it, with `each`.

need.description: What a pattern's `when` runs over: one plain row, made from the data and the agent's task word.

task.description: The agent's word for the work: browse, find, triage, edit…

writes.description: A reader may change the rows.
